mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over a 3-month window signals an easing monetary policy stance, which reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and supports higher S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline in easing episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive excess return in periods where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and cost-push inflation, depressing S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline in periods of sustained low unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline in periods of sustained industrial production declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month window signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which supports S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises >0.25pp AND CPIAUCSL falls >0.2% over 3 months
failure_condition: No significant positive excess return in periods matching the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 400K units signals weakening residential demand, which reduces construction-related earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline in periods of sustained low housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 50K persons signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive excess return in periods where PAYEMS growth exceeds 50K/month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below $300B signals reduced precautionary balances, which increases household spending and supports S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline in periods of sustained low real savings (t-test p > 0.05).
